purpose: Epona - SPECT/PET Review and Epona - SPECT/PET Compare: Slicer modules for reading SPECT/PET with CT/MRI (fusion, MIP, windowing, spherical SUV ROIs, ruler) plus optional AI denoising filters that run Belenos PET Denoise models. Intended for nuclear medicine researchers using Slicer.
summary: Reviewed the catalog entry, CMakeLists, LICENSE, README and the key code paths for AI-filter model downloads (urllib from GitHub releases, SHA-256 checked, cached), torch.load with weights_only=True, and the pip_install of monai/einops on demand. No malicious or concealed behavior seen. Concerns: the catalog entry is minimal and the LICENSE text names "SlicerPETDenoise" rather than this project; the extension installs packages into Slicer's Python environment only after user confirmation, but einops is pinned to 0.6.1 and PyTorch is correctly delegated to PyTorchUtils. Clinical-use disclaimer is present in the README. Not fully verified: the 3 MB icon, runtime behavior, and the remaining ~3,600 lines of Easy_fusion.py and EponaCompare.py.

safety.rationale: Read filters.py download and load paths (urlopen with timeout, .part file, size and SHA-256 check, torch.load weights_only=True) and Easy_fusion.py ensureFilterDependencies; no telemetry or credentials found in the parts read. Model downloads only happen after user action.

environment.rationale: Easy_fusion.py:2882 calls slicer.util.pip_install(requirement) for monai and einops only after confirmOkCancelDisplay; PyTorch is deferred to PyTorchUtils as required. Pinning einops==0.6.1 (FILTER_EINOPS_REQUIREMENT, filters.py:65) could conflict with other packages; not verified.

packaging.rationale: Root CMakeLists.txt sets EXTENSION_DEPENDS 'NA' while the catalog build_dependencies is []; consistent. Easy_fusion/CMakeLists.txt lists the EponaLib files and resources; I did not verify every listed resource exists. EponaCompare imports EponaLib from the sibling Easy_fusion folder, which CMake must ship together.

license.rationale: LICENSE is MIT, copyright Burak Demir, but its grant refers to the software as "SlicerPETDenoise", a different project name; this should be corrected. Downloaded model weights come from SlicerPETDenoise releases whose license was not checked.

soundness.rationale: Code follows Slicer conventions in the parts read: deferred scene work, observer removal in release(), errors logged and reported. Did not run the tests.

utility.rationale: README documents usage, dependencies, clinical disclaimer ('not intended for clinical use'), and offline model setup. Tier 1 is appropriate; tests exist in EponaLib/tests.py but CTest registration is commented out in Testing/Python.

findings.title: LICENSE names a different project
findings.evidence:
Copyright (c) 2025 Burak Demir

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
of this software and associated documentation files (the "SlicerPETDenoise"), to deal
findings.explanation: The MIT grant refers to the software as "SlicerPETDenoise", not PETReviewCompare. The grant is still clear for distribution, but the wording should match this extension to avoid ambiguity about what is licensed.
findings.suggestion: Change the parenthetical to the actual project name or remove it.

findings.title: Hard pin of einops to an old version
findings.explanation: slicer.util.pip_install installs einops==0.6.1 into Slicer's shared Python environment after user confirmation. An exact pin can conflict with other extensions that need newer einops. Only the user's consent covers this, and the pin is not justified in the code.
findings.suggestion: Use a lower bound such as einops>=0.6.1 unless the model code requires the exact version, and document why.

findings.title: Test registration commented out
findings.explanation: Both Testing/Python CMakeLists are commented out, so CTest does not run the module tests. The tests in EponaLib/tests.py run only through the in-app self test.
findings.suggestion: Register the unit tests with slicer_add_python_unittest so CI runs them.

not_checked: Did not read Easy_fusion/Easy_fusion.py or EponaCompare/EponaCompare.py in full (only targeted search and excerpts); the rest of display.py, layouts.py, mippick.py, toolbar.py, overlays.py, registration.py, slicescroll.py, compareviews.py, studyinfo.py, shortcuts.py.
Did not verify that every file listed in Easy_fusion/CMakeLists.txt exists or that the 3 MB fusbanner.jpg and other binary assets are needed in the repository.
Did not verify the license of the SlicerPETDenoise model weights downloaded at runtime, or the upstream repository state at the pinned revision (scm_revision is 'main', a moving branch).
Did not run the extension, its tests, or a Slicer build; no network checks of the GitHub release URLs or SHA-256 values.
Did not check the CI or build results for the catalog entry.
questions_for_author: Why is einops pinned to exactly 0.6.1, and does it conflict with other extensions?
Can the LICENSE copyright text be changed to the PETReviewCompare project name?
Can the unit tests be registered with slicer_add_python_unittest so CTest runs them?
Does scm_revision 'main' get replaced with a fixed commit for the catalog entry?
